question.html:
a

Electrons are emitted from a metal surface when very low intensity light is incident on it. This emission occurs with no observable time delay.

Outline why this observation is not consistent with the wave theory of light.

[2]

b

Light of wavelength 5.2 × 10−7 m is incident on a metal surface and causes the emission of electrons of maximum kinetic energy 1.8 eV.

b.i Estimate, in eV, the work function of the metal surface. [2]

b.ii The emf of the power supply is set at 0.60 V. Determine the speed of the electrons as they arrive at the collecting plate. [3]
